verdict_reason: 30 photos from 4 photographers were on disk and every frame that can be pinned at all pins to Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam. Hard proofs come independently from three of the four photographers: the Thien Quang well with the stele houses and Khue Van Cac, the doctoral stelae standing on stone turtles, the Van Mieu Mon triple entrance gate, Dai Trung Mon on the central path, Khue Van Cac from two different sides, and the Dai Bai Duong interior whose couplet reads '...帝王而後帝王師' (teacher of emperors and kings) with the bronze cranes and a 'HOM CONG DUC' donation box. The remaining frames (red-lacquered Tu Phoi statues, the bronze Chu Van An figure with its classics/history couplets, roof and baluster details, bronze urns, the topiary crane) sit inside those same continuous upload runs and share the same building fabric. The one real outlier is 4360119233, which is a composed 'Hanoi Temples' collage mixing Ngoc Son, the One Pillar Pagoda and a thousand-armed Quan Am.
place_if_genuine: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Girl in yellow silk performing a fan dance on a red carpet laid over stone paving, in front of a red-lacquered round timber column on a stone base with a dark hall behind. Column/base type and red carpet match the Van Mieu bai duong of 4356114856, and the photographer's confirmed Van Mieu frames are in the same trip.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Same fan dancer, wider: red round columns either side, a red silk lantern hanging in the dark hall behind, dark red drape and red carpet. Same performance and hall as 4353039489 and 4353790028.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Large orchid-and-palm arrangement standing on the flagstone floor of a dark timber hall; at the left edge are a bronze gong on a stand and a bamboo tube instrument - the same instruments visible in the music-ensemble frame 4353790028, so the same hall.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Five women in ao dai playing dan tranh, dan nhi, moon lute and a bamboo lithophone on a red-covered platform in a timber-panelled hall hung with painted paper fans, scroll paintings and traditional instruments; CDs for sale on the floor and a sign reading 'TIEN DONG GOP TU NGUYEN / HELP SUPPORT OUR TRADITIONAL MUSIC' (zoomed and read). This is the standard visitor music performance staged in the Thai Hoc house at Van Mieu; the sign itself carries no address, hence the moderate confidence.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Temple interior with a dark red seated statue in a mandarin cap under a gilt dragon canopy in a red-walled niche, blue-and-white porcelain vases, a bronze crane, and gilt-on-red boards legible as 建廟尊聖 ('build the temple, honour the sage') and 大道 plus a 文 plaque - Confucian-temple wording. The statue and canopy match 4504744854, shot by a different photographer in the confirmed Van Mieu run.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: The square Thien Quang well with its white stone balustrade, the two long stele houses flanking it, and the Khue Van Cac pavilion at the far end - the unmistakable third courtyard of Van Mieu.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Rows of tall stone doctoral stelae standing on carved stone turtles under a timber pavilion on brick paving - the 82 Quoc Tu Giam stelae.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Dai Bai Duong interior: red carpet down the centre, gilded altar table, two tall bronze cranes flanking the columns, and legible gilt-on-red couplets '一元磅礴周流天地所生天地小' and '...冕封學教帝王而後帝王師' (teacher of emperors and kings - a Confucius couplet), plus a red 'HOM CONG DUC' donation box.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: A run of red-and-gold altar cases with gilt Han lettering, blue-and-white porcelain vases and red timber columns receding down a hall - same hall fabric and upload run as the confirmed Van Mieu interiors.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Bronze seated scholar in a soft cap with a radiating halo behind him, in a gilded dragon-carved shrine, flanked by couplets legible as '行以體藏以義賢人風節詔...' and '博於史寶於經聖道淵源開...' (history, classics, the sages' Way) - the bronze Chu Van An in the Thai Hoc house; last frame of the confirmed Van Mieu run.

photos.place: Temple of Literature (Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam), Hanoi
photos.evidence: Orange-red brick wall with a white-framed geometric fret lattice window, two bonsai in carved stone planters and a stone water trough in front. The same image appears as a tile in this photographer's own 'Hanoi Temples' collage (4360119233), so it is a Hanoi temple; the brick walling, stone planters and bonsai match Van Mieu's inner courtyards, but nothing in frame is unique to it.

photos.place: UNIDENTIFIED

photos.evidence: Red-and-gold lacquered seated figure in a gilt mandarin cap behind a bronze bird ornament, red timber roof structure above - same altar bay as 4504744854 in this photographer's confirmed Van Mieu run.
